links.outcome: Reading grade level of ACPA educational materials versus recommended guidelines
links.effect: ACPA materials average grade level 10.7 ± 1.8, nearly meeting NIH guidelines but not AMA guidelines.
links.quote: ACPA educational materials are written at an average grade level of 10.7 ± 1.8 with a PEMAT understandability of 82.4 ± 7.0% and actionability of 42.3 ± 17.4%.

links.outcome: Reading level, understandability, actionability of caregiver materials after LLM plain-language modification
links.effect: LLM modification reduced reading level to 8.0 ± 1.2 (P = .0002); understandability 80.5% (P = .5371) and actionability 40.8% (P = .6709) not significantly changed.
links.quote: Modification by LLMs decreased average reading level to 8.0 ± 1.2 (P = .0002) with a PEMAT understandability of 80.5 ± 7.9% (P = .5371) and actionability of 40.8 ± 18.2% (P = .6709).

unlisted_practices: Using LLMs to rewrite existing patient education materials to lower reading level

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the performance of three LLMs (GPT-4o, Gemini, Copilot) in simplifying patient education materials (readability, understandability, and actionability) without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
